evidence: asia-pacific.ts, emerging-markets.ts, europe.ts, japan.ts and north-america.ts each define evaluate() with the same structure: this.currentValueInBaseCurrency ? regionValue / this.currentValueInBaseCurrency : 0, then > ruleSettings.thresholdMax, then < ruleSettings.thresholdMin, then a success branch.
The percent-formatting rule (x * 100).toPrecision(3) is repeated in every branch of every evaluate(), which is 5 files x 3 branches.
getConfiguration() returns the identical object { threshold: { max: 1, min: 0, step: 0.01, unit: '%' }, thresholdMax: true, thresholdMin: true } in all five region files.

getSettings() repeats the same mapping in all five files: isActive: xRayRules?.[this.getKey()]?.isActive ?? true, plus thresholdMax and thresholdMin with only the defaults differing (0.03/0.02, 0.12/0.08, 0.15/0.11, 0.06/0.04, 0.69/0.65).

The constructors in all five region files have the same shape: exchangeRateDataService, i18nService, languageCode, currentValueInBaseCurrency and a region value, plus super(..., { languageCode, key: X.name }). interfaces/rule-settings.interface.ts holds only the Settings type, with no shared behaviour.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is cohesive in concern. All five classes are regional cluster-risk rules, extend Rule<Settings>, and share one Settings interface. But the same rule logic is copied into each region file, so it doesn't live in one place. Each file repeats the zero-denominator guard, the max-then-min threshold comparison, the three-branch translation result with toPrecision(3) percent formatting, an identical getConfiguration(), and the same getSettings() structure. Only the region name, translation ids and default thresholds differ. A change to one of these invariants would have to be made in five places. The module has no shared base class or helper for it. This matches the rubric's fail condition of duplicating a rule or invariant that should live in one place.
